title: Barack Obama: African-American
titleZh: 巴拉克·奥巴马：非裔美国人
credits: Kelly Jean Kelly wrote this story for Learning English. Hai Do was the editor.

sentences.en: VOA Learning English presents America’s Presidents.
sentences.zh: 美国之音英语学习节目为您带来《美国总统》系列。

sentences.en: Today we are talking about Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 今天我们聊聊巴拉克·奥巴马。

sentences.en: He first took office in 2009 and was re-elected in 2012.
sentences.zh: 他于2009年首次就任，并在2012年连任。

sentences.en: Because his presidency is so recent, this program will not try to offer a historical perspective.
sentences.zh: 由于他的总统任期距今不远，本节目将不试图提供历史视角。

sentences.en: But one part of his legacy is already clear.
sentences.zh: 但他留下的一部分遗产已清晰可见。

sentences.en: Obama is the United States’ first African-American president.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马是美国首位非裔美国人总统。

sentences.en: His father was a black man from Kenya; his mother was a white American from the Midwestern state of Kansas.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是来自肯尼亚的黑人，母亲是来自中西部堪萨斯州的白人美国人。

sentences.en: For many Americans, Obama’s presidency was an important symbol in a country that permitted black people to be enslaved.
sentences.zh: 对许多美国人而言，奥巴马的总统任期是一个重要的象征，而在这个曾经允许黑人被奴役的国家里，这一象征意义尤为突出。

sentences.en: And, even after the U.S. Constitution officially banned slavery in 1865, African-Americans have been extremely under-represented in the U.S. government.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使在1865年美国宪法正式废除奴隶制之后，非裔美国人在美国政府中的代表人数依然严重不足。

sentences.en: By 2009, only five African-Americans had ever served in the U.S. Senate – and Obama was one of them.
sentences.zh: 到2009年，仅有五位非裔美国人曾担任美国参议员——奥巴马便是其中之一。

sentences.en: Even many people who did not vote for Obama said his election to the country’s highest office made them proud or hopeful.
sentences.zh: 甚至许多没有为奥巴马投票的人也表示，他当选为国家最高职务让他们感到骄傲或充满希望。

sentences.en: A public opinion survey immediately after Election Day found that two-thirds of Americans believed that the country’s racial conflicts could be resolved.
sentences.zh: 选举日之后立即进行的一项民意调查显示，三分之二的美国人认为国家的种族冲突能够得到解决。

sentences.en: Obama’s parents met as students at the University of Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马的父母在大学就读时相识，那所大学是夏威夷大学。

sentences.en: His father had won a scholarship to study economics.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲曾获得奖学金学习经济学。

sentences.en: His mother went on to earn a degree in math there, as well as a graduate degree.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲随后在那里获得了数学学位，还取得了一个研究生学位。

sentences.en: The two married and had a son, whom they named after his father: Barack Hussein Obama, Jr.
sentences.zh: 两人结婚并生下一个儿子，以父亲的名字为他命名：巴拉克·胡赛恩·奥巴马，小名。

sentences.en: But the couple soon separated.
sentences.zh: 但这对夫妇很快分居。

sentences.en: The older Barack Obama returned to Kenya, where he later died in a car accident.
sentences.zh: 年长的巴拉克·奥巴马回到肯尼亚，他后来在那里因车祸去世。

sentences.en: Barack’s mother went on to marry another man.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克的母亲随后又嫁给了另一个男人。

sentences.en: He was from Indonesia.
sentences.zh: 那个男人来自印度尼西亚。

sentences.en: The family moved to Jakarta, and the couple had a daughter named Maya.
sentences.zh: 这家人搬到了雅加达，这对夫妇生了一个女儿，名叫玛雅。

sentences.en: When Barack was 10, his mother sent him back to Hawaii to live with her parents.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克10岁那年，他母亲把他送回夏威夷，和外公外婆一起生活。

sentences.en: She wanted him to get a good education.
sentences.zh: 她希望他能接受良好的教育。

sentences.en: Barack finished high school in Hawaii, then went on to Occidental College in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克在夏威夷读完高中，随后前往洛杉矶的欧西idental学院就读。

sentences.en: After two years, he transferred to Columbia University in New York.
sentences.zh: 两年后，他转学至纽约的哥伦比亚大学。

sentences.en: There, he completed a degree in political science.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他完成了政治学学位的学业。

sentences.en: But Obama said the best education he received was in one of his first jobs.
sentences.zh: 但奥巴马说，他所接受的最佳教育来自他早期的一份工作。

sentences.en: He worked as a community organizer in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 他在芝加哥担任社区组织者。

sentences.en: He helped people who lived in public housing put pressure on the city government to improve their conditions.
sentences.zh: 他帮助居住在公共住房的人们向市政府施压，以改善他们的生活条件。

sentences.en: Obama later said the work showed him how important it was to understand the legal process.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马后来说，这项工作让他明白了理解法律程序的重要性。

sentences.en: So he entered Harvard Law School.
sentences.zh: 于是他进入了哈佛法学院。

sentences.en: Over the next years, Obama worked as a lawyer, wrote a book about his experience as a person of mixed race, and married Michelle Robinson, a woman he worked with at a law firm.
sentences.zh: 在此后的岁月里，奥巴马作为一名律师工作，写了一本关于自己混血经历的书，并与在律所共工作的米歇尔·罗宾逊结婚。

sentences.en: She and Barack Obama settled in Chicago and had two daughters, Malia and Sasha.
sentences.zh: 他们夫妇俩定居芝加哥，生了两个女儿，分别是玛利亚和萨莎。

sentences.en: When he was in his mid-30s, Obama began his political career.
sentences.zh: 当他三十出头时，奥巴马开始了他的政治生涯。

sentences.en: He was elected three times to the Illinois state senate.
sentences.zh: 他三次当选为伊利诺伊州参议员。

sentences.en: After 10 years there, he won a seat in the U.S. Senate in a landslide victory.
sentences.zh: 在那任职十年后，他以压倒性优势赢得美国参议院的席位。

sentences.en: That same year, Obama attended the Democratic National Convention – the meeting where the party officially nominates a presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 同年，奥巴马参加了民主党全国代表大会——即该党正式提名总统候选人的会议。

sentences.en: Obama was not one of the candidates.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马并非候选人之一。

sentences.en: But the Democrats asked him to make an important speech.
sentences.zh: 但民主党人请他发表一篇重要演讲。

sentences.en: In it, Obama famously talked about how his life story was an American story.
sentences.zh: 在演讲中，奥巴马畅谈了他的个人经历如何成为美国故事的一部分，这一番话广为流传。

sentences.en: He said he was confident the U.S. could overcome its divisions and achieve unity.
sentences.zh: 他表示，他对美国能够克服分歧、实现团结充满信心。

sentences.en: “There’s not a liberal America and a conservative America,” he said. “…There’s not a black America and white America and Latino America and Asian America.
sentences.zh: “这里没有自由派的美国和保守派的美国，”他说，“……这里没有黑人的美国和白人的美国和拉美裔的美国和亚裔的美国。

sentences.en: There’s a United States of America.”
sentences.zh: 这里只有一个美利坚合众国。”

sentences.en: Only four years later, Obama would be elected its 44th president.
sentences.zh: 仅仅四年之后，奥巴马就当选为第44任总统。

sentences.en: I’m Kelly Jean Kelly.
sentences.zh: 我是凯莉·简·凯利。

glossary.def: a way of thinking about and understanding something
believing that government should be active in supporting social and political change
glossary.zh: 自由主义的；主张政府积极推动社会政治变革的

glossary.def: believing in the value of established and traditional practices in politics and society
glossary.zh: 保守的；信奉传统习俗价值的
